A useful detail before you paste

Keep separators short on mobile. Repeated decoration can sound noisy in a screen reader; a blank line or a simple dash is often better for important content.

Click a symbol tile to copy the exact characters shown. Save a selection with the star. If automatic copying is blocked, CopySprig opens a selection window so you can use your device’s copy command.

Aa

Characters, not font files. Your app decides how they look and read. Keep essential text in ordinary letters. Before you paste

Short aesthetic dividers for bios and captions

Each tile copies a complete separator, including its spaces. Start with Four point star divider (─ ✦ ─) for a compact accent, Heart divider (── ♡ ──) for a softer line, or Short line divider (─────) for a plain rule.

Put a divider between two short sections

Place your heading on one line, paste the divider on the next, then add your caption underneath. Check the result in the destination’s narrow mobile view. If it wraps, choose a shorter tile instead of adding more repeated characters.

How do I make my own divider?

Copy a single star symbol or heart symbol and place a few dashes around it in your app. To frame words as well, the text decorator adds matching symbols around each nonblank line.

Why does a divider look uneven after pasting?

The destination chooses the font, character spacing and line width. A separator can look different from its preview here. Try Short line divider or Plain asterisk divider if an ornament displays poorly. For essential content, a blank line or a written heading is easier to read.

Keep a small reference nearby

Download the curated character list as a plain UTF-8 text file. It includes names and a short paste checklist.
